synonyms: ["Alcoholic Nose", "Drinker's Nose", "Flushed Nose", "Red Nose", "Nasal Flushing", "Nose Redness", "Rhinophyma Nose", "Gin Blossom Nose", "Red Nose Alcohol", "Red Nose And Alcohol"]
conventional_description: Rhinophyma is an advanced form of rosacea that causes the skin on the nose to thicken, become red and bumpy, and develop prominent oil glands. It typically occurs after years of untreated or severe rosacea, more often in men. The exact cause is not fully understood, but chronic inflammation and dilation of blood vessels play a role. Diagnosis is usually made by a dermatologist based on appearance, and it is not caused by alcohol alone, though alcohol can worsen flushing.
conventional_treatments: Conventional treatment aims to reduce inflammation and reshape the nose. Options include topical medications like metronidazole or azelaic acid for milder redness, oral antibiotics such as doxycycline to control inflammation, and isotretinoin for severe cases. For the thickened, bumpy tissue, laser therapy, dermabrasion, or surgical shaving can remove excess skin and improve appearance. These approaches manage symptoms but do not address the underlying tendency to flush and develop new lesions.
tcm_understanding:
TCM understands rhinophyma primarily through the Lung and Stomach organ systems. The Lung opens into the nose and governs the skin, so when excess heat accumulates in the Lung - often from spicy foods, alcohol, or emotional stress - it rises upward along the channel and reddens the nose. The Stomach channel also runs across the cheeks and nose, and its heat can surge upward after heavy, greasy meals, causing flushing and breakouts.
Over time, if this heat is not cleared, it can sink deeper into the Blood, making the redness persistent and leading to fragile, visible capillaries. When the heat intensifies further, it can transform into Toxic-Heat, producing painful pustules and abscesses. In chronic, long-standing cases, the heat and emotional stress cause Qi and Blood to stagnate, resulting in the thickened, nodular, dark purple nose characteristic of advanced rhinophyma.
This is why TCM doesn't treat all rhinophyma the same way. A nose that flushes after a glass of wine and then fades is a different pattern than one that stays permanently red with knobby growths. By identifying the exact pattern - Lung Heat, Stomach Fire, Heat in the Blood, Toxic-Heat, or Qi and Blood Stagnation - the practitioner can choose herbs and acupuncture points that target the root imbalance, not just the skin.
classical_quote: 「肺胃素有积热，又饮酒食辛辣，热气上蒸，故令鼻准赤。」
classical_translation: "When there is long-standing accumulated heat in the Lung and Stomach, and one drinks alcohol or eats spicy foods, the heat steams upward, causing the nose tip to become red."
classical_source:
Sheng Ji Zong Lu (《圣济总录》)  ,  Nasal Diseases (鼻门) 									·

tcm_diagnosis:
A practitioner begins by asking what makes the redness better or worse. If the nose and cheeks flush after spicy food, alcohol or a stressful moment, and the redness comes and goes, Lung Heat is the likely starting point. The tongue is often red with a thin yellow coat, and the pulse feels rapid and floating.
When Stomach Fire is present, the practitioner looks for digestive clues: constant thirst, bad breath, a craving for cold drinks or constipation. The facial heat tends to flare after heavy, greasy meals. The tongue is red with a thicker yellow coat, and the pulse is rapid and forceful, reflecting heat rising along the stomach channel.
As the condition lingers, Heat in the Blood makes the redness stick. The practitioner notices a darker, more persistent erythema with tiny visible blood vessels. The face feels hot even when the person is calm. The tongue may be red with red spots and a thin yellow coating, and the pulse is rapid, wiry, and slippery, showing that heat has moved deeper.
If pus-filled bumps, abscesses and sharp pain appear, Toxic-Heat is the main concern. The practitioner checks for yellow, tender lesions and asks about any feverish sensation. The tongue is red with a greasy yellow coating, and the pulse is slippery and rapid, pointing to a more severe inflammatory stage that needs urgent cooling.
In long-standing cases, Qi and Blood Stagnation creates a thickened, bumpy, dark reddish‑purple nose. The practitioner feels the skin texture and looks for a dusky tongue with purple spots. The pulse is often wiry or choppy. This picture tells the practitioner that poor circulation and stagnation are now driving the skin changes.

patterns.symptoms: ["Facial redness, especially on the nose and cheeks", "Flushing worsens with heat, spicy food, or alcohol", "Dry mouth and thirst", "Red tip and edges of the tongue"]
patterns.worse_with: Spicy food, Alcohol, Emotional stress, Hot weather or sun exposure, Fried or greasy foods
patterns.better_with: Cool compresses on the face, Drinking plenty of water, Avoiding spicy food and alcohol, Cooling herbal teas (e.g., chrysanthemum), Rest and relaxation
patterns.why_this_happens: In TCM, the Lung opens into the nose and governs the skin. When excess heat accumulates in the Lung-often from spicy foods, alcohol, or emotional stress-it rises upward along the channel to the face. This heat dilates the tiny blood vessels and causes the characteristic redness, flushing, and papules on the nose and cheeks.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, especially the tip, with a yellow dry coating; possible prickly papillae on the front third. Pulse: rapid (shu), slippery (hua), and may feel overflowing (hong) at the right cun position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Spicy, greasy, and fried foods, along with alcohol and emotional stress, generate internal heat that rises to the face through the Lung channel, worsening redness. Cooling foods, hydration, and rest help clear that excess heat and allow Lung Qi to descend, reducing the upward surge that dilates facial blood vessels.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid spicy, greasy, and fried foods, as well as alcohol, which all generate internal heat. Eat cooling foods like cucumber, pear, and watermelon. Practice gentle stress management such as deep breathing or walking in nature, and protect your face from excessive sun or heat.

patterns.better_with: Cool or cold drinks, Light, non-greasy meals, Resting after meals
patterns.why_this_happens: Your Stomach is like a furnace that cooks food into energy. When that furnace overheats-often from rich, spicy meals, alcohol, or stress-excess Fire builds up inside. The Stomach channel runs directly up through the cheeks and nose, so this internal heat surges upward along that pathway, reddening and inflaming the skin on your face, especially around the nose.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body, often with central prickles, and a thick, dry yellow coating. Pulse: rapid, slippery, and forceful, especially strong at the right middle position.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Spicy, greasy foods and alcohol directly add more heat to an already overheated Stomach, and emotional stress can cause Qi to stagnate and turn into Fire. Cooling foods and drinks help douse that internal Fire, while lighter meals and rest allow the Stomach to process food without generating excess heat.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat plenty of cooling, moistening foods like cucumber, watermelon, pear, and leafy greens. Avoid alcohol, coffee, spicy dishes, and fried or greasy foods that stoke Stomach Fire. Eat smaller, regular meals rather than large feasts, and try to wind down after eating rather than rushing around.

patterns.better_with: Cool compresses on the face, Drinking cool water or chrysanthemum tea, Resting in a cool, quiet room, Eating cooling foods, Gentle breathing exercises to calm the mind
patterns.why_this_happens: Heat in the Blood means the blood itself has become overheated. In rhinophyma, this often develops after repeated episodes of Lung Heat or Stomach Fire that eventually drive the heat deeper into the Blood level. The overheated blood causes the tiny vessels in the nose to dilate and become fragile, leading to a persistent, dark-red discoloration and visible broken capillaries. Because Heat consumes Yin and fluids, the skin may feel dry and the redness tends to worsen at night when Yin is naturally lower.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with red spots or prickles, thin yellow dry coating. Pulse: rapid (Shu), wiry (Xian), slippery (Hua), and forceful.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Spicy food, alcohol, and emotional stress all generate internal Heat, which directly feeds the Blood Heat and makes the nose redder. Hot environments add external Heat, while night-time is when Yin energy should dominate; if Yin is already damaged by Heat, the imbalance worsens and the redness intensifies. Cooling foods, compresses, and rest help drain excess Heat and protect Yin, soothing the overheated blood vessels.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Eat plenty of cooling foods like cucumber, watermelon, and mung beans. Avoid alcohol, spicy dishes, and fried foods which add heat. Protect your face from strong sun and keep stress levels low with gentle activities like walking or meditation.

patterns.why_this_happens:
When Heat accumulates in the body without being properly cleared, it can deepen into a toxic form of Heat. In the nose, this manifests as painful pustules and abscesses, because the nose is the opening of the Lung channel and a gathering place for facial Yang Qi. The toxic Heat damages local tissues, causing redness, swelling, and pus formation.
This pattern represents a more severe stage of rhinophyma, where the body's internal Heat has become so intense that it produces visible pus-filled lesions and significant discomfort.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: red body with prickly thorns, dry yellow coating. Pulse: rapid, forceful, and slippery.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Toxic-Heat is an accumulation of intense internal Heat that has transformed into a deeper toxicity. Alcohol, spicy foods, and stress generate more Heat, adding fuel to the fire. Cooling foods and rest help clear Heat and allow the body to resolve the toxicity. Cool compresses directly soothe the local skin inflammation.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid alcohol, spicy and fried foods, and prolonged sun exposure. Drink plenty of water and eat cooling foods like cucumber and mung beans. Keep the face clean and avoid picking at lesions.

patterns.why_this_happens: In the chronic, advanced stage of rhinophyma, long-standing heat and emotional stress cause Qi to stagnate. Over time, this stagnant Qi fails to move Blood, leading to blood stasis in the nose. The result is a thickened, dark purplish-red, nodular nose because sluggish blood flow deposits waste and causes tissue overgrowth.
patterns.tongue_and_pulse: Tongue: dark purple body with stasis spots, distended sublingual veins. Pulse: wiry and choppy.
patterns.why_triggers_reliefs_work: Emotional stress and anger cause Liver Qi stagnation, which directly worsens blood stasis in the face. Alcohol and spicy foods generate internal heat that further congeals blood flow. Cold weather constricts blood vessels, making stagnation worse. Conversely, warmth and gentle massage encourage blood circulation, while stress reduction helps unblock Qi flow, allowing stagnant blood to move.
patterns.diet_and_lifestyle: Avoid alcohol, spicy, and greasy foods which generate internal heat and worsen stasis. Practice stress management techniques like meditation or gentle yoga to prevent Qi stagnation. Gentle daily exercise such as walking promotes smooth blood circulation. Protect the face from cold wind and excessive sun exposure.

faqs.question: Can TCM cure rhinophyma?
faqs.answer: It can significantly reduce redness, flushing, and pustules, and in many cases stop the progression. For early stages, complete resolution is possible. For advanced, thickened tissue, TCM can soften the skin and prevent further growth, but existing overgrowth may also need conventional reshaping procedures. The goal is to correct the internal imbalance so the nose does not worsen.

faqs.question: How long until I see results?
faqs.answer: Most people notice less facial flushing and fewer breakouts within 2-4 weeks of herbal treatment. Redness and heat sensations typically diminish over 4-8 weeks. If the nose is already thickened and bumpy, expect gradual softening over several months. Consistency with herbs, acupuncture, and diet is essential.

faqs.question: Do I have to give up alcohol and spicy food completely?
faqs.answer: In the early stages of treatment, yes - alcohol, spicy food, and very hot drinks are major triggers that fuel internal heat. After the condition stabilizes, occasional small amounts may be tolerated, but many people find that avoiding these triggers is key to staying clear long-term. Your practitioner will guide you based on your pattern.

faqs.question: Will acupuncture help the redness?
faqs.answer: Yes. Acupuncture points on the face and body help clear heat from the Lung and Stomach channels, cool the blood, and improve local circulation. Many patients notice that their nose feels cooler and looks less red after a session. Regular treatments reinforce the effects of herbs and diet.

faqs.question: Is TCM safe alongside laser treatments or surgery?
faqs.answer: Generally, yes. Herbs and acupuncture can be used before and after conventional procedures to reduce inflammation and support healing. However, if you are taking blood-moving herbs (like Hong Hua), inform your surgeon, as they may slightly increase bleeding risk. Always tell both your TCM practitioner and dermatologist about all treatments you are receiving.

faqs.question: What diet changes do I need to make?
faqs.answer: Focus on cooling, light foods: cucumber, watermelon, pear, mung beans, chrysanthemum tea, and plenty of water. Avoid spicy, greasy, fried foods, alcohol, coffee, and excessive red meat. Eating smaller, more frequent meals can also help if you have Stomach Fire with digestive symptoms. Your practitioner may tailor advice to your specific pattern.

faqs.question: Does TCM work for advanced rhinophyma with thickened skin?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it requires patience. The herbs and acupuncture for Qi and Blood Stagnation are designed to gradually soften hardened tissue and improve blood flow. While the nose may not return to its original shape without surgery, TCM can halt further thickening, reduce the purple tone, and prevent new nodules from forming.

research.title: Treatment of Rosacea from the Lung and Spleen Theory
research.description: This review discusses the TCM pathogenesis of rosacea and rhinophyma, emphasizing the roles of Lung Heat and Spleen Dampness. It presents clinical cases where modified Pi Pa Qing Fei Yin and spleen-fortifying herbs reduced facial erythema, papules, and nasal thickening, supporting a pattern-based approach.
research.periodical: Zhang Y, et al. (2020). Treatment of Rosacea from the Lung and Spleen Theory. Traditional Medicine Research, 5(6), 1-8.
